quests.title: No Bed Between Here and the Bay
quests.description:
Sentry Vrak has stood at Grom'gol's south gate for three years telling people that the road is the whole of the accommodation between here and the harbour. She has stopped enjoying saying it.

She keeps a tally because nobody asked her to. Eleven went south this month and nine came back through her gate, and she does not know which two are still walking.
quests.accept_text:
Walk it. Not the first mile - down to the ford where the Veilfall crosses the road, which is where the raptors have been working, because that is the one place on the road a person has to slow down.

Ten of them, if you can manage ten, and look at the stones in the ford while you are standing in it. If anyone went into that water I want to know before their mother does.
quests.turn_in_text:
Nothing in the ford. Good.

No. Not good. I wanted them in the ford, because a man in a ford is a man I can account for. Two people walked off the end of my tally and the road has nothing to say about it, and that is the part of this post nobody warned me about.

quests.title: The Road Does Not Keep Itself
quests.description:
Road-Ganger Dubo's gang keeps the Vine Road cut, and the Gurbashi pay for it, because the arena needs a crowd and a crowd needs something to walk on.

Bloodvine takes a cut road back in nine days. He has measured it. He will tell you the number the way other people tell you their children's names.
quests.accept_text:
You will want to know how a road works, so. There is a camber on it - the middle sits high and the water runs off the sides, and if the water does not run off the sides you have a river with ambitions. Kerb stone holds the camber. Vine comes through the kerb.

Cut me six good lengths of it out of the kerb line and put eight of the green adders off the verge while you are down there. They nest in the drainage. They should not be in the drainage.
quests.turn_in_text:
You cleared the drains.

I did not ask you to clear the drains. I explained the drains. Those are different and I am aware they are different.

Where you're from they would have been somebody else's drains, I expect. Down here the road is whoever last cut it.

Right. Bexxil is up on the apron and she has been wanting a name. I will give her yours, and you can decide afterward whether that was a kindness.

quests.title: Somebody Has Already Written Your Name
quests.description:
Tout Bexxil works the board, and the board is in Booty Bay, nailed up inside the tavern where the Baron can see it and pretend not to.

She entered you this morning. She opened you at a price, the price moved twice before noon, and she is not going to tell you either number. What she wants now is a card worth watching, and the Gurbashi have been thinning it themselves.
quests.accept_text:
The drovers are running undersized stock into the crates and signing it in at weight. Thin card, thin crowd, thin money, and I am the one holding paper on a thin afternoon.

Nine of the drovers and four of their tallies. And before you ask why I bet on somebody I have never watched fight - that is the entire reason. Nobody down here knows what you people can do. Not knowing is where my money lives. Nobody has a form line on you lot, and the rim likes that in a fighter more than it likes a fighter.
quests.turn_in_text:
You did it where they could see you.

The price came in. Do you understand what that means? The price coming in is the money going out, and the money was going to come to me.

I have had to put my own purse on you to hold the line. That is not a compliment. That is a relationship, and you did not agree to it, and neither did I.

quests.title: Staked
quests.description:
Bexxil's own money is on the board now, which has changed what she is. A tout can walk away from a bad afternoon. A backer cannot.

There is one piece of paper left between you and the sand, and it goes to the Gurbashi gatehouse, and the gate crew do not take a goblin's word for anything that is not a weight.

objectives.label: Put the chit in Zul'tamo's hand

quests.accept_text:
Take the chit up the apron to the broker and put it in his hand. Not on the table. In the hand, and stand there while he reads it.

Seven of the gate crew will try to stop you getting that far, because that is the job they are paid for and they will do it without any feeling about it. Do not take it personally and do not take it slowly.
quests.turn_in_text:
She has filled the chit out in her own hand. Name, weight, reach, standing - and in the box where a house goes she has put outsider.

Zul'tamo reads it out flat, the way he would read a weight.

'Outsider. Good. Not from here is a column on this sheet, not an insult - we have had it longer than you have been in the world and it prices better than any other line on it. You are on the list. Come down when the drums start.'

quests.title: Ordek Asks About Rain
quests.description:
Ordek Fenn has had a drying rack and a tarp on the dry shoulder of the Veilfall lip for two years, and he sells to Grom'gol through whoever is walking north.

He is pleased to see you in a way nobody else in this jungle has been, and he does not make a performance of it. He has a question he has been saving and it is not about the jungle.
quests.accept_text:
There is a band of moss along the lip where the spray reaches and nowhere else - seven good handfuls would do me the season. Mind the leeches in the slack water under the pool. Eight of them and the shallows are yours.

And while you are gone, think about this for me: where you're from, does the rain come in a season, or does it come all year? Everything I know about a plant assumes a wet month and a dry month. If it rains all year where you came from then half of what I know is local, and I would very much like to find out which half.
quests.turn_in_text:
A season, then. Good. That is one thing I do not have to throw out.

Now the moss. Look at where you picked it - only the band. Only where the water reaches.

That is not a jungle plant. That is a waterfall plant, and there is one waterfall. I have been selling it to the camp as common for two years and pricing it accordingly, and I have just made myself considerably poorer by asking you a question.

quests.title: Somebody Lights It From Inside
quests.description:
After dark the sheet of the Veilfall glows. Ordek has watched it do that from a camp stool for two years and told himself it was the water doing something clever with the moonlight.

Water does not do that. Lamps do that. Lamps mean wicks and oil and somebody trimming them, and that means the cave behind the fall has had people in it the entire time he has been sitting outside its door.
quests.accept_text:
The panthers work the lip at dusk, which is the honest reason I have never walked round to look - seven of them between my rack and the notch, most evenings, and I am a man with a trowel.

Go round to the mouth. That is all. Stand at it and come back and tell me whether there is a door there, because I have spent two years deciding there was not one.
quests.turn_in_text:
Carved steps. Carved steps and a lamp bracket with oil still in it.

Two years. Two years I have been camped at somebody's front door, selling their moss, and I never knocked, and I told myself a story about moonlight so I would not have to.

You knocked. I am going to need a moment about that and I would rather have it alone.

quests.title: It Has a Name. Several.
quests.description:
Attache Zul'jana is the only person inside Grom'gol's fence who is from this jungle, and she has spent three years listening to a garrison name things.

The camp calls it the waterfall cave. The Zul'Rath who keep it have four names for it and which one they use depends on which terrace they are standing on. She will give you one. She is keeping the others and she does not feel she owes you an explanation for that.
quests.accept_text:
Zul'Dakai. That is the one you may have, and it means the stone the water argues with - you can carry that word north and the camp can put it on a map and be pleased with itself.

Each terrace has a name stone set into its lip. Bring me four of them. The mistcallers will not let you stand on a terrace long enough to read one, so you will have to go through eight of them first, and I am not going to pretend to you that I like asking for that.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four stones, four names, and the fourth one is not a name for the cave at all.

It is a name for the water. And it is the same word the Gurbashi use for the sand on their arena floor - the exact same word, same two sounds, and one lot means a river and the other lot means a killing-ground.

I have known both of those words my whole life and never once put them next to each other. Go and ask the gatehouse what they think they are saying.

quests.title: The Font, and the Argument With It
quests.description:
The shrine terraces are the part a visitor notices. The Font at the east end is where the Zul'Rath do the actual work, and the work is measurement: a knotted cord let into the water every morning and read against the one from the morning before.

Three years ago the fall changed. More water, and in the wrong month. They have been arguing with it since, and the argument is written down.
quests.accept_text:
Five cords and the chamber they are read in. Nothing else - leave the shrine alone, it is not ours and it is not yours.

The spraywater will come at you in the Font because the Font is what they are made of; eight of them will clear you a quarter of an hour to work in. Read nothing. Carry it. I will do the reading.
quests.turn_in_text:
Up. The fall has been up since the year the sky changed over and it has not come back down once.

I am not carrying this to Overseer Mokra. She will ask what it means, and the honest answer is that the river is now draining a country that was not there to drain, and that the water has to be coming off something, and that nobody has gone to look at what.

She would write it down. That is the problem. She writes everything down.

quests.title: The Veilspeaker Will Not Be Argued With
quests.description:
The Veilspeaker has reached a conclusion about why the fall is wrong, and the conclusion is that somebody is standing where nobody should stand.

The somebody is Ordek Fenn. On a Tuesday, a party of his shrinekeepers came up the shoulder and took the drying rack apart, piece by piece, without hurrying and without saying one word to him.
quests.accept_text:
I want you to understand what I am asking and that I have thought about it for four days.

He is on the south shore of the plunge, and he has decided my tarp is why his water is wrong, and he is not going to be talked out of it because I have tried. I went in. I went in on the Wednesday with a jar of oil as a gift and I came out again without saying a word, and the difference between us is that he is right about the shoulder being his and I am right about having nowhere else.

Go down and end it. Please do not tell me it was quick.
quests.turn_in_text:
It was not quick. Thank you for not saying it was.

I have his bracket. The one from the mouth, with the oil still in it. I am going to put it on my own rack and that will be the whole of the monument, because nobody is coming to make him one.

And I am still going to have to decide about the camp. Killing the man did not move the shoulder.

quests.title: What Watcher Garza Has Not Sent
quests.description:
Watcher Garza was posted out of Grom'gol to sit on the one road up onto the Mosh'Ogg Shelf and report what comes down it. She has sent nine reports in eleven weeks.

All nine say the same thing, and the reason they say the same thing is that in the second week she put the spyglass - signed for, numbered, drawn against her name - down the notch, and everything since has been written from memory and a good imagination.
quests.accept_text:
The rockthrowers pick up anything that catches the light and they put it on the midden behind the camp, and I have been looking at that midden through nothing at all for nine weeks.

Eight of them, and bring me five things off the pile. Not the bones. The made things. If the glass is in there it is in there with a brass collar and my number stamped on the collar, and if it is not in there then I am going to have to write a tenth report that says something different from the other nine.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fifth one. There it is, brass collar, number and all, and I have had eleven weeks of being quietly sick about it.

Now look what it was lying against. That is a crate nail. Square cut, stamped, Gurbashi arena stock - and arena stock does not come up this road, because this road goes nowhere but up.

So the ogres have been trading with the gate, and that is a real report, and the only way to file it is with the ten weeks attached. I asked you to tidy a midden and you have handed me a confession.

quests.title: One Road Up, and They Know It
quests.description:
The Mosh'Ogg hold the shelf because the shelf has mesas on every side and exactly one notch through them, and they were the people standing nearest the notch when it mattered. That is the whole of their claim and they have never pretended otherwise.

Garza's tenth report is going to be a bad one. She would like at least one number in it to be going the right way before she attaches the ten weeks to it.
quests.accept_text:
This is not strategy and I am not going to dress it as strategy. It is bookkeeping.

Ten of the maulers off the approach and six of the spellgorgers out of the clearing on top, and then walk into the clearing itself so that somebody has actually stood in it this season. A post that reports a camp it has never entered is a post that is guessing, and I have done eleven weeks of guessing and would prefer to stop.
quests.turn_in_text:
They moved the camp. Six feet.

Six feet, west, and then they stopped and put the fire back in the middle of it and sat down. That is not a rout. That is a shuffle, and it is the entire history of that rock in one gesture - they have been shuffling on it for generations and holding it the whole time, because nobody has ever wanted the notch badly enough.

I have been watching a people shuffle for eleven weeks and calling it a garrison in writing.

quests.title: A Week of Ulua's Nets
quests.description:
Netsetter Ulua has set nets in the Snapjaw Marsh her whole life and her mother set them before her, in the same water, off the same landing.

She does not want help. She wants somebody to pull her lines for one week, she is not going to say why, and her hands are shut most of the way into fists and have been since the cold month.
quests.accept_text:
Eight lines, out past the gangplank where the water stops moving. Pull them, bring the catch in, and reset them the way you found them and not the way you think would be better.

Seven of the crocolisks have been taking the nets with the catch still in them, which is the only part of this I will complain about out loud.

And do not tell anyone in the Bay you did this. I sell into the Bay.
quests.turn_in_text:
Eight, and you reset them right, which I did not expect.

Something I will ask you and then we will not discuss it again. Where you're from - is there standing water? Brackish, slow, the kind that does not go anywhere?

And does anyone fish it.

I am not making conversation. I would like to know whether this is a trade that exists in more than one place, in case it stops existing in this one.

quests.title: Somebody Did Not Want To Be Found With This
quests.description:
You cut it out of a crocolisk's gut, which is not where paper goes.

It is a betting slip. Salt-stiff, gone brown at the folds, and still perfectly readable: a fighter's name, a round, and a price. You do not know the fighter. You do know that a price that good is a price somebody was offered because they knew something, and that there is exactly one reason to carry a slip like this out into standing water and stand in it.
quests.accept_text:
The handwriting is small, fast and very legible, and there is a goblin up on the arena apron who writes exactly like that.

Take it to her. Go back along the marsh track to the gangplank first and look at the water either side of it, and go through eight more of the crocolisks on the way, because whatever else is in that stretch of marsh is inside one of them.
quests.turn_in_text:
She knows the hand before she has the slip the right way up, because it is hers.

'That card was pulled. That fighter never went on the sand - I wrote this, I priced it, and then the house scratched the round and I bought the paper back in. All of it. I counted it back in.'

She turns it over twice.

'Where in the marsh. Exactly where. Because there is one reason to walk a dead slip out into water, and it is so that nobody ever finds you holding it.'

quests.title: Anticlockwise
quests.description:
Gatehouse Broker Zul'tamo's father kept this list and his grandfather cut part of the wall it is nailed to. He does not care who wins. He cares that the list is right.

What he will give you before you go down is the one thing nobody in the Bay can sell you: how the place is built, and why it is built that way.
quests.accept_text:
You come down the stair at the top of the ring and you will see you can only go one way round it. People tell visitors that is tradition. It is masonry. The two faces that would let you choose were never cut, three generations back, because the mason did not want the order to be a choice.

First is Vek'tar, and his round is the one the rim likes, because it ends in a number of minutes everybody can count. Go at him and keep going - under a third he will drink the fight back out of you.

Then the grate. Mok'tal keeps a fire under that floor and it never lapses, and he closes off whatever you were going to use to answer it. Nobody has ever made a patient fight of Mok'tal and come up the stair.
quests.turn_in_text:
Two off the list.

The drum crew had you on the long count and they lost money on it, which I enjoyed. They keep a separate count for fighters who came through from somewhere else - you open too fast, all of you, every time, and it is not an opinion, it is a drumming problem. They have had to learn a second rhythm since your lot started coming down that stair.

You did not open too fast. I will tell them. They will not believe me.

quests.title: The Handler Is the Fight
quests.description:
The rim has noticed whose money is on you, which means the third station has been changed. The pair-handlers have put Jin'sha in with Rakjan, and they do that when the house wants a round to stop being predictable.

Zul'tamo tells you this flatly and without apology. It is not his decision and it is on his list, and both of those things are true at once.
quests.accept_text:
Rakjan is loud and Rakjan is not the problem. The handler behind him is the problem, and if you spend the round on the big one you will die to the small one and the rim will say you fought the wrong man, which you will have.

Then Zul'gar. Understand what he is before you go at him: he is not a fighter, he is a door. He stands in the mouth of the passage to the hall and there has been somebody standing in that mouth every day for three generations - the job has a name and the name is older than the family that holds it. Three swings, all of them enormous, and one of them takes your armour off you. Hitting him harder does not change that arithmetic.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four crossed off.

Now a thing I should not tell you and am going to. The house does not open the centre gate more than once in a season. It has never had to. There is no rule about it - there has simply never been more than one in a season who got as far as the dead end.

It has opened twice this season. The first one was eleven days ago and nobody has said his name since, and I have begun to wonder whether the gate is a prize or a tidying-up.

quests.title: The House's Own
quests.description:
Four rounds have made Bexxil's stake worth a great deal more than she paid for it, and she has done what anybody holding paper that good does: she sold most of it on.

What is left of her position is the awkward half. It pays if you go the distance with Jen'shala and lose honestly. It pays very little if you win. She has decided to tell you this to your face, which is not kindness and is not quite its opposite either.
quests.accept_text:
Here it is, flat. I laid off four fifths of you this morning at a price your rounds made me, and the fifth I kept pays best on a long loss. Eleven minutes and down. That is my number.

And I am telling you because I cannot buy eleven minutes off somebody who does not know I want them, and because you would have found out, and because I would rather be the one who said it.

She is one and four at once - she drinks the fight back out of you AND she takes your armour off, and she is the house's own, and the house has never put her on the sand to lose. Go down. Do what you are going to do. Collect in the Bay, not here.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Quiet Man counts it out without looking up, which is how you know it is the real number and not the one Bexxil would have preferred.

'She is not ruined. She is annoyed, which on her is nearly the same shape.'

He squares the coin off with one finger.

'The board has a field for where a fighter came from. It has had that field since before the Baron. Since you lot started walking down that stair it is the only line on the sheet anybody argues about, and somebody has to sit down tonight and re-price it, and it will be me.'

He finally looks up. 'Do not come back for a season. Let the number settle.'

quests.title: What Scrip Thinks the Drums Are
quests.description:
Scrip has never been a mile out of the cove. He has heard the arena drums come down the cape on a still night - twice, both times in the wet month - and he has built an entire theory out of it.

The drums are gorilla hide. One of them is bigger than a boat. He is completely certain and he is prepared to pay in the only currency he has, which is knowing which crates on the pier are not nailed down.
quests.accept_text:
Right, so you go up the road and you count them. I want how many drums, how wide across the top, and what they are made of, and do not just say gorilla because I know it is gorilla, I want it written down by somebody who was there.

Eight of the big apes, the ones they call drumhides - that is a clue, that is practically the answer - and five bits of hide so I can feel it. And stand on the flat bit in front of the gate so you can tell me how many people fit.
quests.turn_in_text:
No.

No, you have looked at the wrong ones. Crocolisk. You are telling me the big drums are crocolisk belly off the marsh and the gorillas are the little ones round the edge, and that is - no.

He folds the hide scrap up small and puts it in his shirt anyway.

'Was anyone down there from off-world? Like you? Because Hobb says the ones who came through always lose the first round, every time, and I said that can't be right, and he said ask someone who'd know.'

He is waiting. He is nine.

quests.title: A Nail With a Number On It
quests.description:
You turn it over. It is a crate nail - square cut, flat headed, the kind that goes into shipping timber and nothing else - and it is stamped with a run number.

You found it on the Mosh'Ogg Shelf, up a road that goes nowhere except up. Numbered nails come in runs. A run means a clerk, and a book, and a line in the book that says where the crate went.
quests.accept_text:
There is only one man in this jungle who would recognise a run number on sight, and he is in Booty Bay behind a desk, and he will be unbearable about being asked.

Go through the brutes on the way down off the shelf - eight of them hold the notch, and they are the ones with the nailed timber in their camp, which is the part you want to be sure of before you say any of this out loud to a clerk.
quests.turn_in_text:
Clerk Bexx looks at it for less time than it takes to say the number.

'Mine. That run went out of this office, to the gate, under weight, signed. It should be at the bottom of a pit full of broken crates behind an arena.'

He puts it down very precisely on the manifest he was working on.

'It is not. It is in an ogre midden on a shelf, which means somebody is opening my crates before the gate counts them. And do you know what I am angry about? The stamp. The stamp is legible. A legible stamp is a thing a person can audit me with, and I have spent eleven years making sure nobody could.'
